findings: SOURCE QUALITY: fandom wiki pages (welcometothegame.fandom.com) returned HTTP 402 to WebFetch, so wiki-derived facts below come from search-engine summaries of those pages and from guide sites; treat them as medium confidence. Steam store pages and the Memeburn review were fetched directly (high confidence).

[WTTG1] Welcome to the Game, Reflect Studios, released June 15 2016 (Windows/macOS). Premise: sit at a PC, browse the deep web, find 8 hidden keys that assemble the URL of a Red Room, solve puzzles, finish mini-games to avoid being hacked, and avoid kidnappers. https://store.steampowered.com/app/485380/Welcome_to_the_Game/

[WTTG1] Clock: the Red Room is only online 30 days, and getting hacked costs calendar days. Tools: A.N.N. browser, a Notes app (keys plus site visit times; a hack can wipe notes), anti-hacking software. https://memeburn.com/gearburn/2016/07/welcome-to-the-game-review/

[WTTG1] Hack interrupts, each a timed mini-game: Kernel attack (retype code-like phrases before time runs out, easy) and DOS attack (rotate arrows to route a moving block to the end, ramps hard and causes frequent hacks). Reviewer complaint: link-clicking becomes tedious and novelty fades. https://memeburn.com/gearburn/2016/07/welcome-to-the-game-review/

[WTTG1] Modem/connection: per fan-wiki talk-page snippet, resetting the IP via the modem temporarily disables hacking attempts but is a long procedure that leaves the player vulnerable (low-medium confidence). Players also asked for faster modem resets in a 2017 casual-mode request. https://welcometothegame.fandom.com/wiki/Talk:Welcome_to_the_Game/@comment-67.159.138.177-20180318033503/@comment-105.103.214.215-20200614183302

[WTTG1] Hacker Mode DLC (Nov 10 2016): endless chain-puzzle mode built from the DOS and Kernel mini-games plus a CLOUDGRID mode, with points spent on upgrades (skip level, extra life after a failed hack, permanent time boost, 30 s freeze). https://www.dekudeals.com/items/welcome-to-the-game-hacker-mode

[WTTG1] Kidnapper: he tracks you the longer you are online. Cue: a small location arrow beside the WiFi icon top-right for a few seconds, plus ambient knocking or creaking. Counter: leave the PC, switch off the computer and the light, stay still and silent; he walks past the window. If alerted (mic noise, light left on, phone ringing) he jumps through the window = instant game over. Inside cues: footsteps, moved furniture, something dropped; a misplaced dining-room chair is the one visual tell; his search sequence is randomised. Trigger timing is disputed (after 3 keys vs random on key pages). https://welcometothegame.fandom.com/wiki/Kidnapper?oldid=6799 and https://steamcommunity.com/app/485380/discussions/0/3108018684262723320

[WTTG1] Breather: teases by phone (heavy breathing or threats; the desk phone ringing is the warning), then attacks the front door. Counter: turn to the door, hold the knob shut through repeated kicks until he gives up and retreats into the bushes. The door/window check (look at the porch, hold the door) is called a key mechanic. https://welcometothegame.fandom.com/wiki/Breather?oldid=8229

[WTTG1] Endings: reaching the Red Room plays a live snuff-film cutscene as the default ending; two other endings exist (details not found). The house itself is a single room set (a dining room, window, front door), so tension comes from sound, darkness and interruptions, not from a map. https://welcometothegame.fandom.com/wiki/The_Dining_Room (House page) and the fandom Endings page referenced in search results

[WTTG2] Welcome to the Game II: Steam release Apr 3 2018 (the brief says 2017; Steam says 2018). Atmospheric horror/strategy/puzzle. Search 3 tiers of deep wiki for 8 hashes to decrypt the shadow-web browser; simulated OS with browser, notes and a software store; hack neighbours' WiFi to dodge police tracking; earn a currency and buy WiFi boosters and motion sensors; explore your apartment building while hunted. Player is a reporter investigating a missing woman. https://store.steampowered.com/app/720250/Welcome_to_the_Game_II/ and https://www.giantbomb.com/wd/3030-61971 (via search)

[WTTG2] Time structure (fan wiki, medium confidence): 6 in-game hours = about 3 real hours, roughly 10 PM to 4 AM with 1 in-game minute = 30 real seconds. Sites are minute-gated: ~36 always-open sites, timed sites open only in windows such as xx:00-14, xx:30-44, xx:45-59; ~29 never-available bait sites whose broken links trigger instant hacks (which can earn Backdoor money); a Rule of Three on wiki 2 gives the URL of wiki 3. https://www.magicgameworld.com/?p=17184

[WTTG2] Economy (guide sites): in-game currency DOSCoin (fan wiki: starts at 35, UI says 10); VPNs 1-5 earn coins from 'green' positions and cut hack chance (L5 about 99 %); Dongle 3 upgrade tiers for faster connection; Backdoor costs 1 coin per use and steals coin when it blocks a hack; Key Cue software (300+ coins) marks key pages; about 250 coins needed to finalise the ending tunnel. Opening a key page and every 3 hacks add a hidden difficulty point; 3+ points open the window (fan claim). https://prodigygamers.com/2018/04/11/welcome-to-the-game-2-tips-and-trick-to-beat-the-game , https://www.magicgameworld.com/?p=17186 , https://steamcommunity.com/app/485380/discussions/0/6790907198725742898

[WTTG2] Shops: zeroDAY market (software) and Shadow Market (hardware, delivered by a drone drop in the alley; failing to pick up the package or open the door kills you). Gear: Police Scanner, Motion Sensor, Motion Alert (remote earpiece with sound alarm), Blue Whisper (shows whether the hitman is in your room while you are out), WiFi dongles. https://welcometothegame.fandom.com/wiki/Welcome_to_the_Game_II?oldid=4234 (via search) and https://www.magicgameworld.com/?p=17186

[WTTG2] Police/SWAT: tracks your WiFi at random; each network has a detection rate (WEP worst, WPA middle, WPA2 best); siren audio swells as they close in; counter is hopping between low-detection networks and using the scanner; reconnecting does not help. https://www.magicgameworld.com/?p=17186

[WTTG2] Hitman (Lucas): spawns after the first or second key page or after about 11:00, roughly one visit per hour, rotating with Noir and power-outage events. Cues: footsteps and lockpicking. If the door is locked he picks it (faint cue, about 10 s to hide); if unlocked, instant death. Routine: lock door, switch off bedside and closet lights in set order, shut down the PC to protect coins/notes, hide in closet or bathroom shower, stay silent; after he leaves, turn lights back on at once or Noir spawns. Sources give the surname Kumiega, not 'Holmes' (brief's name is unverified). https://www.magicgameworld.com/?p=17189 , https://steamcommunity.com/app/720250/discussions/1/1694919808753974648

[WTTG2] Noir (masked figure): appears at window, balcony, doors, hallways, or at random while roaming; contact is death. Counter: stay calm, back away, turn your back, count to 30, never run at him; spawns more with more keys and in dark areas during outages; a link that does nothing is the cue to check the window. https://www.magicgameworld.com/?p=17116 , https://prodigygamers.com/2018/04/11/welcome-to-the-game-2-tips-and-trick-to-beat-the-game

[WTTG2] Breather (alley only): footsteps/laughter cue; walk backwards, hide behind a side door, hold the door shut when pushed (timed to his exhale). Dollmaker: triggered by visiting his site (doll noise, power cut); fix via the maintenance room, then use a Lolpy Disc on the lobby computer to find the woman and place the doll head on her door. Keys raise threat frequency. https://prodigygamers.com/2018/04/11/welcome-to-the-game-2-tips-and-trick-to-beat-the-game , https://www.magicgameworld.com/?p=17189

[WTTG2] Confirmed apartment-building spaces: bedroom (bedside light, closet with light as hiding spot), bathroom shower (hide), balcony, front door with lock, stairwell, lobby (computer), maintenance room (restores power), alley, a 'bottom door'. https://steamcommunity.com/app/720250/discussions/1/1694919808753974648

[WTTG2] Win/lose: lose by death from any threat (hitman, Noir, Breather, SWAT) or failing the package pickup; win by gathering 8 hashes across three wikis and paying the final cost. Achievement 'The Professional' = beat the game without buying anything. https://www.magicgameworld.com/?p=17189

NOT FOUND IN ANY SOURCE (do not rely on): an elevator, apartment number 803, a place called 'the Zone', and a peephole in WTTG1 or WTTG2. Searches for lobby/elevator returned only unrelated games. These director ideas are original to this project, which is fine, but they are not WTTG facts.

[WTTG3, bonus, third-party summary] The motel sequel includes a slot-machine app that converts its coin into a separate gambling currency, a Reputation stat, hired services (hackers, hitmen), a bomb-maker triggered by visiting his site, a permadeath 'Normal Plus' mode, and five promised endings. WTTG itself has therefore already flirted with gambling-on-the-deep-web. https://youtubesummary.com/summary/NJvb35Q2VRs

TENSION RECIPE (synthesised from the sources above): (1) sound is the first warning and light the second, so the player reacts before seeing; (2) two jobs compete for attention (productive search/hack vs. watching door, window, phone); (3) the correct answer to each threat is different (stay still, hold door, lock + hide, back away + count), so no single reflex works; (4) darkness is both safety and danger (lights off hides you, lights off after Lucas invites the masked figure); (5) hidden timers and rotating random events (Lucas / Noir / outage) keep players from solving the schedule; (6) death is instant and total, so every cue is respected; (7) more progress (keys) means more threat.

ideas: 1. THE LATE RIDE (evening between Nights). WTTG hook: the second game's apartment building and its hours-long night structure. JackID version: after a paid Dawn and the Night Card pick, the intermission lever becomes TAKE THE LIFT; elevator.ride('down') (src/world/types.ts:63) drops the player to a small flat built like THE UNDERNEATH (far-offset room). The Evening is 60-90 s of sim time with four stations: phone, door, desk, bed. Using the bed ends it and calls openFloor() (run.ts:1486), riding back up. Nights 1 is a no-threat tutorial; Night 8 skips it (topside, run.ts:1996). A SKIP EVENING button forfeits only the Dream draw, so nothing soft-locks. Why fun: it splits the loop into gamble-by-day and survive-by-night and gives a breath after Dawn; fits because the gap, the gate pattern and the elevator prop already exist.

2. HEAT AND THE ANSWERING MACHINE (escalating deadline threat). WTTG hook: hidden difficulty points that rise with hacks and key finds, and the Breather's phone calls before the door. JackID version: a run-level HEAT 0..6 computed by a pure module like checkpoints.ts: +1 per missed Watch tithe, +1 per rescue loan, +1 per broken seal, +1 for paying with under 5 % margin, -1 per overshoot tier claimed from favoured upward, -1 decay per quiet Night. The home phone plays messages in the Collector's voice (reuse PhoneCallState, rescue.ts wire format) that escalate courtesy -> reminder -> final notice -> 'we are on our way' by heat, and say plainly how many Nights remain on the quota ladder. Why fun: the player reads their own risky play as a visible threat meter, so greed has a cost beyond coins; fits because every input already exists in run state and the HUD Plan strip can show HEAT.

3. THE KNOCK (door, chain, peephole, lights; three visitors with three different counters). WTTG hook: each threat needs a different answer (stay silent and dark, hold the door, lock and hide, back away and wait), and the player juggles two things at once. JackID version, original visitors: THE LEANER shoves the door in 3 beats, each with a 0.4 s audio telegraph; hold-to-brace on the beat. THE LISTENER stands outside; lights off and no input for 8-12 s, and running, using the phone or opening the Jar counts as noise. THE PICKER scrapes at the lock; with the chain/deadbolt off you have about 10 s to get behind the bed, the deadbolt adds 6 s. A peephole look reveals which visitor it is but a lit room leaves a shadow under the door (bad against the Listener), so information costs risk. Two-things-at-once: counting the day's receipts at the desk (a Dream bonus) needs the lights on, while the Listener needs them off. Handled visitors add Rest points; a failed one costs a toll (8 % of the pocket, capped by the House Limit) or +1 Heat, and a Soul Mark at Heat 4+. Never lethal on Nights 1-6. Why fun: sound-first, readable, skill-based tension that is orthogonal to slot RNG; fits because Calm Mode, subtitles and the dread events already exist.

4. THE FINAL KNOCK (a missed quota becomes a lethal visit with outs). WTTG hook: instant death if the door is unlocked, and preparation items that tell you something is coming. Director requirement: the mafia kills the player on a miss. JackID version: replace the instant trapdoor at run.ts:1963 with a three-step scene (peephole -> door -> hide) once per miss. Existing outs stay first: false_bottom (shortfall under 10 % forgiven) and rope_ladder (Overtime Watch). Then survival needs a prepared home (chain, deadbolt, a hiding spot bought in the home shop) AND the correct counter for the visitor type chosen by Heat. Survived: the shortfall is added as loan quota and one Soul Mark is lost (or one Overtime Watch); failed: fall() as today (run.ts:2017). Fully telegraphed (messages on the machine, HEAT readout, audio cues with a visual twin) so the death is earned, not random. Why fun: it turns the existing sudden trapdoor into the best scare in the run and makes the home shop matter.

5. THE HOME SHOP WITH DELAYED DELIVERY. WTTG hook: a software store and a hardware store (door locks, motion sensors, scanner, alert earpiece), hardware arriving by an alley drop you must collect. JackID version: spend Tickets (economy.types.ts:12; earned by tithes and overshoot tiers) on 6-8 home items priced 2-6 Tickets: Chain (+1 shove absorbed), Deadbolt (+6 s Picker warning), Rug Sensor (footsteps cue 3 s earlier), Dimmer (lights off instantly), Peep Cover (a look leaves no shadow), Radio (shows next Night's visitor type and Heat tier), Spare Key Hook (lets one Final Knock out reset). Orders placed tonight arrive in the dumbwaiter next evening, so planning one Night ahead is the skill. Items are ModProviders with x.home.* hooks (run.ts:583). Why fun: it gives Tickets a second sink with a build identity (door build vs sensor build vs radio build); fits as data plus a few readers.

6. DREAMS (the luck-card layer that feeds progression). WTTG hook: the quiet reward for surviving the night; adapted so the evening produces LUCK BONUSES. JackID version: using the bed scores REST 0-3 (visitors handled, calm, time left) and opens a seeded Dream draw (2 cards at Rest 0-2, 3 at Rest 3; offer = hashSeed(seed,'dream',night) exactly like Night Cards, nightCards.ts:1-12). Cards are one-Night boons: Lucky Mint (luck +3 via the 'luck' hook), Windfall (payout.flat), Deep Pockets (overshoot.mult x1.25), Extra Pull (+1 pull via x.run.pullsAdd), Hot Hand (jackpot.mult), each paired with a small cost on the risk side. Rest 0 gives a one-Watch 'Restless' luck -1 debuff. Progression: collect 3 Dreams of one family for a permanent small Foundations node (luck +1 style, upgrades.ts:338) or an Obol multiplier, using the set pattern in charms/sets.ts. Why fun: players choose between safe and risky luck every Night and have a reason to survive the evening well; fits because every effect is an existing hook.

7. THE JAR (hidden wealth against the House). WTTG hook: items and coins you can lose to an intruder unless you protect them (the hitman makes you shut down the PC to protect coins and notes). JackID version: at the desk move up to 25 % of the pocket into a Jar that is NOT counted in houseWealth (run.ts:1965 reads coins + debtPaid), so it dodges the House Takes Notice quota floor (run.ts:2009-2015), but those coins cannot be staked on the floor and come back only at the next evening. A Picker or Leaner that gets through steals 30 % of the Jar. A voice-only spouse leaves a request note ('bring home at least X', read against ledger.carried, run.ts:1990); meeting it adds a Dream card. Why fun: it is a real risk/return decision that interacts with the wave-47 wealth tuning and gives the home layer an economic stake; fits because houseWealth is a single clearly defined number.

8. THE TALLY HUNT AND AUDIT PING (timed key search plus the hack-style interrupt, on the casino floor). WTTG hook: 8 keys hidden across the deep web, sites open only in minute windows, and timed hack mini-games (retype code, route arrows) that interrupt searching. JackID version: BASE_RUN_NIGHTS is 8, so one hidden Tally per Night (8 in a run). Each Night one Tally appears on a random open machine for a 12 s window inside a seeded Watch (watchEvents.ts / spotlight pattern). Interacting spends one pull and starts an Audit Ping: a 6-8 s retype-the-receipt-number or arrow-routing mini-game while the Watch clock keeps running. Success banks the Tally (one Dream re-roll each); fail smudges it and adds +1 Heat. Eight Tallies unlock the true ending path (endingPathId exists, run.ts:686-688) or a meta unlock. Offer the Audit Ping as an opt-in AUDIT NIGHT risk card first so it cannot clog fast play. Why fun: it gives the gambling Watch a second, skill-based objective and a run-long collection goal; fits because the 8-Night structure and timed-event tooling already exist.

ORIGINAL-IP CHECKLIST for naming: do not use or paraphrase Kidnapper, Breather, Noir, Lucas, Dollmaker, Red Room, Shadow Web, deep web wikis/hashes/keys-as-URL, DOSCoin, zeroDAY, Shadow Market, Blue Whisper, Key Cue, Backdoor, VPN-as-income, 'Rule of Three', Lolpy, Amelea, Clint Edwards. Suggested original vocabulary: Leaner, Listener, Picker (visitors), Tally, Audit Ping, Jar, Dream, Rest, Heat, Evening, dumbwaiter drop, final notice.
risks: Research confidence: fandom wiki pages could not be fetched (HTTP 402), so threat, modem and ending details rest on search summaries and guide sites; the director's WTTG vocabulary (elevator, apartment 803, 'the Zone', peephole, 'Lucas Holmes') is not supported by any source found and Lucas is Kumiega in guides. WTTG2 shipped in 2018, not 2017. Re-verify anything we plan to cite publicly; because the crossover is original-IP, none of it blocks the design.

IP risk: scripts/check.mjs:19-20 enforces an original-IP rule (bans 'clover' and 'chest'); the same discipline should apply to WTTG terms. Keep mechanics inspired, names, scripts and text original (see the checklist idea).

Scope: a new world room, a new Evening phase, visitors with audio/visual cues, a shop and a Dream layer is large. ShiftPhase (shift.types.ts:24) is saved and networked (protocol.ts:66, :164-165); prefer an Evening sub-state inside 'intermission' gated like nightCardGate rather than a new ShiftPhase, and decide up front that co-op/versus skip the Evening or run it host-authoritative.

Pacing: 7 evenings of 60-90 s add 7-10 minutes to a run that already has 3-4 Watches of 150-210 s per Night (schedule.ts:105-112). Mitigate with SKIP EVENING, a no-threat Night 1, short evenings on early Nights, and never blocking OPEN THE FLOOR forever (timers on sim time, auto-resolve like the Night Card 20 s auto-pick).

Fairness of lethal events: the Final Knock replaces an instant trapdoor with a skill check; if any cue is audio-only, or Calm Mode / reduce-flashing players cannot read it, the death will feel cheap. Every cue needs a visual and subtitle twin, Calm Mode must lengthen timers and strip jump scares (director.ts HorrorSettings), and the Final Knock must be fully telegraphed by HEAT and messages.

Economy and balance: luck is clamped to +-30 but payout.mult goes up to x1000 (modifiers.types.ts:76); Dream boons stack with charms, Night Cards, overshoot tiers and sets. The Jar can undo the wave-47 House Takes Notice wealth floor (run.ts:1964-1966, schedule.ts wave 47 notes) unless capped; Tickets gain a second sink that changes the value of tithes. All of this needs the sim (scripts/sim/run.mjs) before tuning; the director already spent many waves tuning reach per Night (N1 93 % ... N8 about 22 %).

Determinism and saves: all rolls must be hashSeed(run.seed, night, ...) like hotline.ts:20-22 so Daily seeds and benches stay reproducible; timers must be sim-time (wave 67 fixed-step clock) or byte-identical bench runs break; new RunSave fields must be optional with defaults (run.ts:380-400) so older saves load; no Math.random / setTimeout in game code (check.mjs rules).

QA tooling: the bot clicks run.openFloor() in the intermission (scripts/qa/bench.mjs:1530) and would stall or be refused by a new home gate; add an auto-resolve path for bots and headless runs, and add pure-rule tests for heat, visitor outcomes and Dream offers in the style of scripts/tests/nightCards.test.mjs.

Merge conflicts: another team is editing src/game/run.ts, nightCards*.ts, checkpoints.ts, buffs/* and hud.ts right now (git status). Keep new logic in new files (src/game/home/*, src/world/home/*) and limit changes to run.ts to three hook points (:1492 gate, :1963 Final Knock branch, :2000 evening start).

Tone and rating: WTTG is a stalking/violence horror; the current game uses light horror with a Calm Mode (director.ts:1-6). A home visit with a spouse and a death-on-miss mafia must stay within that tone (implied threat, no gore) and be fully localised EN/TR; the check rule on prose literals (check.mjs, rule 3) will fail the build on untranslated text.

Design coherence: the Hollow Door (a once-per-run secret portal with its own duel, run.ts:1817) and rescue loans already express 'the House's dark side'; the Evening must not duplicate them. Suggest the Collector/Lords lore stays the single antagonist family and Mira the single human voice, so the home layer deepens the existing story instead of adding a rival one.
